description:
⚠️ **SEQUENCED BEHIND `73-canonical-router-live-transport` (2026-08-12).** The CANONICAL router is the Erlang one, and its `default_transport()` is `fun(_Backend, _Payload) -> {error, <<"no live transport configured">>} end` — `apr_translate.erl`'s own docstring says a backend is *"recognised, reported, never dialed"*, and `translation/crates/wire/Cargo.toml` declares only `serde` + `serde_json`, no HTTP client. So **widening the LiteLLM dispatch adapter for a router that cannot dial has no observable effect at run time**: every new rung reaches the same refusal the existing ones do. The work here is still correct and still wanted — it is what makes the router USEFUL once it can dial — but it must land AFTER `73`, or its acceptance criteria can only ever be proven against a transport-less stub and the breadth will read as shipped capability it is not. Do not treat this as a blocker on `73`; it is the consumer.

---

Phase B (provider-router adapter breadth). Widen the Python/LiteLLM dispatch adapter past the 2-of-7 native-wire vendors it dials today (anthropic/gemini text — see docs/litellm-dispatch-adapter.md §'Which vendors actually became dialable'). Write the pending-adapter rungs for replicate / elevenlabs / minimax / runway / luma in the modalities agora ROUTES them for (`PAID_PROVIDERS`), turning honest `pending-adapter` refusals into real rungs ONLY where LiteLLM genuinely dials that modality — never forcing a translation nobody verified. The adapter stays BELOW the transport boundary and behind `AGORA_LITELLM=1` (off by default), so every hand-built differentiator (always-completes terminal rung, per-request pre-dial ceiling, `unpriced`!=free, KCB manifest) is untouched, and the byte-for-byte Erlang/Python corpus (`apr_conformance_SUITE`) stays green. agora gates on `make check`; the router gates on `make check-provider-router`.

userStories.title: Add the LiteLLM rungs that genuinely dial the modality agora routes
userStories.description: For each of replicate/elevenlabs/minimax/runway/luma, add the LiteLLM-backed rung ONLY in the modality `PAID_PROVIDERS` routes the vendor for, where LiteLLM actually dials it — each with a round-trip test proving the pair. Where LiteLLM cannot serve agora's routed modality (the docs §'Which vendors' gap table: replicate chat-only, minimax no-video, elevenlabs binary-stream mismatch, runway/luma no-adapter), the rung stays an honest `pending-adapter`, never a fabricated dial.
acceptanceCriteria: Every rung added dials the modality agora routes the vendor for (per `PAID_PROVIDERS`) and round-trips through a stand-in LiteLLM in a test; a vendor/modality LiteLLM does not cover keeps resolving to `pending-adapter` (an honest refusal), matching the anti-fabrication rule in docs/litellm-dispatch-adapter.md.
The docs/litellm-dispatch-adapter.md gap table is updated to reflect the new coverage vs the still-uncovered pairs; `make check-provider-router` green.

userStories.title: Re-prove the hand-built guards below every new rung
userStories.description: Per docs/router-hand-built-behaviours.md §2.3, the always-completes invariant, the pre-dial ceiling refusal, and `unpriced`!=free must be re-asserted whenever a Phase-B adapter adds a rung. Prove that turning the adapter on for the new vendors cannot make a zero-budget request spend, and that `resolve_all` never raises.
acceptanceCriteria: A test counts the calls a stand-in LiteLLM receives and asserts a request over the ceiling is refused BEFORE the transport is reached for every new rung (the `TestTheCeilingStillRefuses` shape), and an unmapped model stays `unpriced` (refusable, not priced zero).
The always-completes terminal placeholder rung and `resolve_all` never-raises invariant hold with the new rungs present; `make check-provider-router` green.

userStories.title: Default surface and byte-for-byte corpus unchanged
userStories.description: The adapter stays keyed off `AGORA_LITELLM=1` (off by default, lazy import, optional extra) so the Python router's default surface is exactly what it was, and `apr_conformance_SUITE`'s Erlang/Python byte-for-byte equality still holds — re-running `capture_python_surface.py` must reproduce the corpus byte for byte.
acceptanceCriteria: With `AGORA_LITELLM` unset the router's surface is unchanged (a missing extra degrades the ladder with an actionable message, never denies service); the new rungs are reachable only with the variable set.

Re-running `provider-router-erl/test/apr_conformance_SUITE_data/capture_python_surface.py` reproduces `python-surface.json` byte for byte (the `AGORA_*` variable is scrubbed by the suite); `make check` green.
